cross_market_insights: AU SERPs are thin and off-intent: Sydney is dominated by Australia-as-destination content for inbound visitors (Scott Dunn, a Tripadvisor thread holding four slots, kimkim); Melbourne and Brisbane return destination lists (Boutique Events Group, BudgetAir, a thin keyword site). Nobody in AU serves an Australian couple flying out with a structured itinerary.

London is commercial: tour operators and an airline (Audley, Virgin Atlantic, Trailfinders) sell sample trips; editorial results are single-destination itineraries (The Knot Europe, a 21 day UK blog).

Template intent exists but goes to Pinterest, Etsy fillable checklists and TheGooDocs (images pack in Sydney, Pinterest rank 8 and 'Honeymoon Itinerary Template' related search in London). No travel brand with real planning expertise owns a printable honeymoon template.
Length questions show up in PAA and related searches ('2 week honeymoon cost', '7 days', '10 days'); jauntaround says many couples take 7 to 10 days. A two week sample answers a real query cluster.

Gap nobody covers: the structure of a honeymoon (arrival and rest, two bases, a travel day placed deliberately, a slow finish before the flight home) plus the invisible work (transfers, buffers, wet weather, documents, Smartraveller) from an Australian departure point.

Volumes: DataForSEO returned no AU volume for all five keywords; Zoho plan figure is AU 10 / US 140. Treat this as a hub page whose value is internal linking for 13 planned itineraries, not traffic on its own.
payload.recommended_angle: A destination-agnostic honeymoon itinerary template plus a two week sample built on structure, not on named hotels: arrival and rest, two bases joined by one deliberate travel day, a slow finish, and the work behind each day (transfers, buffers, wet weather, documents). Written for Australian couples flying long haul, and built as the hub that every destination honeymoon itinerary links up to.
